s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, ulcerative, purpuric skin lesion with rapid growth and extension
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: Lesion first developed in March 2014
Rapid growth and extension occurred in June 2014
Lesion is 30 × 25-cm in size
Centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral lesions
Involvement of left anterior scalp, left parietal scalp, left forehead, and left lateral cheek
Extension to right frontal and right parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and extension of a purpuric lesion with central ulceration and bleeding, consistent with aggressive vascular tumor

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral lesions, similar to Kaposi's sarcoma presentation

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly growing, ulcerative skin lesion, which can be a feature of Merkel cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive, ulcerative skin lesion with lymphadenopathy absence, consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral lesions, similar to cutaneous B-cell lymphoma presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells, which stained positively with CD31, is highly suggestive of a vascular tumor, and the large size and rapid growth of the lesion are consistent with angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Kaposi's sarcoma can present with similar vascular lesions, the lack of lymphadenopathy and the specific immunohistochemical profile do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Merkel cell carcinoma typically presents as a solitary, firm nodule and does not usually exhibit the vascular features seen in this case.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical and histological features do not support a diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, which typically presents with different types of skin lesions and has distinct immunophenotypic markers.

rejected.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical and histological features do not support a diagnosis of cutaneous B-cell lymphoma, which typically presents with different types of skin lesions and has distinct immunophenotypic markers.
